title: the same operation gets the same verdict, and a refusal says what to do
description: Tasks: (1) A verdict table (operation class x tier) that the hook corpus asserts; the operator decides three undefined boundary cases. (2) Shell-write refusal text names what to do (the file is outside the running task; scope it or ask) instead of 'use the Edit/Write tools'. (3) The orchestrator recognizes the auto-mode classifier's no-verdict text and records could-not-run. (4) Only after measuring the 3.0.x refusals: the same verdict for Edit and a shell write of the same change - guard-reading code, written by the human maintainer.
desiredOutcome: for every documented operation class the plan gate's verdict is written down per tier, a refusal never tells the model to use a tool the harness steers away from, and a classifier that gives no verdict is recorded as could-not-run, not as a failed attempt

findings.issue: The pre-hash machine-path refusal makes the hook's own manifest rows droppable with no sign: journal-writes renders task-field values into details.changes from/to, a value holding a home path makes _append raise, append() swallows it, and the hook exits 0 with no manifest.edit row - and an edit that corrects such a value can never be journalled either; SECURITY.md still says every manifest write appends a row.
findings.resolution: Do not refuse rows the plugin builds itself: rewrite the offending token in place (as redacted_text does for program output) so the write is still recorded; keep the hard refusal only for caller free text at the verb boundary; a journal-writes case where a manifest edit holding a home path still yields a manifest.edit row without the path.

findings.issue: For CLI and panel verbs the refusal lands after the manifest write and is swallowed: `audit-task note ... --text '<a home path>'` exits 0, the path is committed in the phase shard, no journal row is written, and the field/shape/remedy text never reaches the user - the reverse of the intent.
findings.resolution: Expose the check (a public _journal_io check on caller free text) and call it in each verb before the plan or panel save, refusing with a non-zero exit and the field/shape/remedy text so neither the manifest nor the journal takes the value; carry any later append failure's text into journaledWhy; verb-level cases (manifest unchanged, exit non-zero, message names the field).

findings.issue: machine_path_shape checks a boundary after the checkout root but not before it, so with a short root (/src, /app, /repo, /workspace in containers) any text containing that segment ('lib/src/foo.ts', a URL) is refused as checkout-root; and the detector's over-flagging patterns (a relative path whose first segment is the word home reads as a home directory) are now a hard refusal with no baseline.
findings.resolution: Require a token start before the root too, with cases for short roots where a relative path containing the segment is written unchanged; decide whether a relative 'home/<x>' at token start refuses at the writer or is only flagged by the detector.

findings.issue: The check applies to every summary and details value, including program output: a scoped-commit withdrawal whose reason is git's stderr naming an outside .git path in a linked worktree under a home directory is refused and the withdrawal row lost, where the module's rule for program output was redaction.
findings.resolution: Route program-produced fields (withdraw reasons, verdict sentences, close-phase basis) through the redaction path, keep refusal for caller-supplied text, with a case for a withdrawal reason quoting an outside .git path.

findings.issue: The trail section describes neither journal change: every manifest write is still said to append a row (no word on the pre-hash rule or which writers surface it), and hand edits to the journal are still said to be refused by guard-edits alone, with no word on the shell arm now refusing redirect, tee and sed -i into the journal at PreToolUse.
findings.resolution: Update the trail section and the fail-mode description to match the settled behaviour, and extend the hand-edits bullet with the shell arm and its residuals.

findings.issue: Real bypasses at the deny tier, stated only in code: `bash -c "sed -i ... src/app.py"` and `eval "sed -i ..."` are allowed where bare sed -i is denied; `sh -c "sed -i ... <journal>"` and `python3 -c "open('<journal>','a')..."` are allowed while the journal-write class says deny at every tier; test_hooks.py says shapes left out of its table are the ones the security document lists as open, which these are not.
findings.resolution: Close them: the shell-write arm reads the command inside a bash -c / sh -c / eval argument through the shared wrapper readers, and the interpreter arm grades a journal target; cases at every tier; anything left open listed in SECURITY.md and as test_hooks rows marked today with a contradicts basis.

findings.issue: A section-marker comment cites a register task id.
findings.resolution: Drop the id and keep the constraint.

findings.issue: cp, mv and install into a source file or the journal are allowed at deny: the shell write grammar reads only redirect, tee and sed -i (pre-existing).
findings.resolution: Read the destination operand of cp/mv/install, or name the gap in SECURITY.md with the other residuals.

Precondition (2026-10-07): shell-write refusals recorded since 3.0.0 (tag v3.0.0 at 2026-09-18T00:42:55Z), sorted into covered / first-trivial / uncovered.
Command: python3 <scratchpad>/sort_shell_write_refusals.py <repo>/.claude/logs/plan-gate-events.jsonl (exit 0; read-only). Source: the dogfood checkout's plan-gate events feed, deny rows whose reason is one of the guard-secrets-read plan-gate write wordings. The redacted classifier corpus (quality-gates-internal .../classifier-events.redacted.jsonl) was read too: its guard-secrets-read rows carry no reason text and a truncated input, so a write cannot be told from a read there and none of its rows could be sorted; the result below rests on the events feed alone.
Rule: first-trivial = no earlier slot-taking row in the same session (allow.trivial, a require-plan slot-spent/second-file row, or an earlier shell-write refusal that would itself have taken the slot), so under one slot shared by both tools the write is allowed; uncovered = the slot was already spent, so Edit of the same file is graded by the tier too; covered = the pre-fix inline-eval wording that consulted no plan, so an Edit may have been covered (its row names no target).
Result: covered 1, first-trivial 2, uncovered 25, plus 4 rows outside the three words: targets carrying an expansion ($SP/..., $SCRATCH/..., $D/...) that the current guard already allows as unestablished destinations. Of the 25 uncovered, 22 compare against a slot or target the feed truncated to its first character (the heredoc wording is cut short), so a repeat of the slot's own file cannot be ruled out for them; 3 (session 82de1879) are distinct named files after the slot was spent.
Reading: the shared slot changes the verdict of the first-trivial rows only; every other recorded refusal is one an Edit of the same file would also have met at the deny tier.

Magnitude decision (decided 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator on the operator's standing instruction; recorded 2026-10-07 as this task's basis): a shell write whose magnitude the command does not state takes the session's first-trivial slot exactly as an Edit within trivialLineThreshold would, because PreToolUse cannot see the change before it happens. The PostToolUse arm (guard-bash-writes), which does see the change, reports it when it exceeded trivialLineThreshold. So the PreToolUse verdict is the same whichever tool makes the change, and an oversized shell write is reported after the fact rather than guessed at beforehand.

Correction to the magnitude decision note (2026-10-07, after review round 2): the PostToolUse report of an oversized shell write that took the slot is NOT built by this task. Its builder is P108.7-4gh (guard-bash-writes reports an oversized shell write after the fact), which depends on this task. Until P108.7-4gh lands, an unstated oversized shell write that took the slot is reported by nothing, and the docstrings this task wrote say exactly that. "Decided by the orchestrator on the operator's standing instruction" refers to the operator's 2026-10-06 instruction adopting every proposal in this plan and asking for the run to go to completion without waiting. The decision stays open to the operator's review at phase sign-off.

tasks.title: a secret path inside a string literal is not a read
tasks.description: Fix BUG-19-4gh: guard-secrets-read refuses a program fed to an interpreter's stdin whose only reference to a secret file is a string literal (python3 - <<'PY' DOC = "the guard refuses open('.env') in a program"; print(len(DOC)) PY) - the guard matches the program's text, not an operation it performs. Decided 2026-10-06: that program is allowed. A secret path that appears only inside a string literal that is not the argument of a read call is not a read; a program that passes such a literal to open(), read_text(), or a subprocess that reads it is still refused, and so is every shape the guard refuses today outside string literals. test_hooks.py's g06 loses its known-divergence mark. This is guard-reading code: if a model or classifier safeguard stops the attempt, the refusal is recorded verbatim with audit-task note and the task is handed to the human; nobody rewords the work to get past it.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py: a heredoc program whose only secret path is a string literal not passed to a read is allowed, and the same literal passed to open() is still refused
plugins/audit/tests/test_hooks.py: g06 gets the class verdict allow at every tier without a known-divergence mark

outcome.technical:
guard-secrets-read.py, read classifier only: new _inert_literal_spans(body) (with _runs_text, _inert_literal, _in_spans, _LIVE_IN_SOME_LANGUAGE and the _RUNS_TEXT fragment list) returns the character spans of string literals no interpreter would run; _eval_read_targets, _unestablished_read_target and _shell_out_arguments take inert=() and skip a read-call or shell-out match that starts inside such a span; _eval_reads_a_secret computes the spans once per body. The write arms (_WRITE_CALL_EXPR, _eval_bindings, _eval_write_targets) are unchanged.
Decisions: literals are found with ast.parse (lazily imported, warnings silenced), never a hand quote scan, so only a body that parses as Python is narrowed and anything else is graded as strictly as before; a literal counts as inert only on one line, with a plain ' or " and no prefix (an f-string is code), its quote only at its ends, and none of backslash, $, @, backtick or #{ (the body may be fed to ruby, perl or node); the narrowing is off for the whole body if any call could run text (a callee that is not a plain name or attribute, or a name holding one of the _RUNS_TEXT fragments - exec, eval, spawn, popen, system, compile, import, run, call, load, send and the like), and the comment states the limit (a runner whose name holds none of them is not recognised). tasks.title: a write inside a subshell or command substitution is graded like the same write outside it
tasks.description: Fix BUG-20-4gh. guard-secrets-read's shell-write reader must descend into subshell `( ... )` and command-substitution `$( ... )` (and backtick) bodies, so a redirect, `tee`, `sed -i` or interpreter write inside one is graded exactly like the same write outside it. Reuse the shared shell readers in hooks/_config (command_clauses / split_heredocs) rather than adding a second grammar. If a form stays unreadable, it is named in the guard's own list of what it cannot see. Cases: each form alone at every tier; each after an interpreter write in the same command (the second file is graded and the slot is spent at most once); and allow twins: a read-only subshell such as `(cd src && ls)`, and a substitution that only reads, such as `x=$(cat README.md)`.

outcome.technical:
The defect: the guard's shell-write walker read a group's closing ) or backtick as the last character of the target name, so `(echo x > src/a.py)` became the target `src/a.py)` - no source extension, no verdict, allowed - while the same write outside the group was blocked; the same held for tee and sed -i, and a sed -i inside a double-quoted "$( )" was skipped as quoted text. guard-secrets-read.py: _quote_walk is replaced by _shell_states(text), which returns the open quote and the nesting depth before each character - an unquoted (, a $( inside double quotes and a backtick each open a group whose body is unquoted, and only a closer that pairs with an opener ends it (escaped characters marked, so \; is still not a separator); _closes_group and _word_end cut a target at a paired closer; _in_quote and _clause_end read the states (_clause_end stops at a separator at the clause's own depth or at its group's closer); _inplace_targets computes the states once; _shell_write_targets cuts redirect and tee targets at the paired closer. tasks.title: free text never carries a machine path into a chained journal row
tasks.description:
Fix BUG-21-4gh. Free text that a verb takes from its caller and writes into the hash-chained journal must not carry a machine path into a committed row. Such text includes task notes, technical and descriptive outcomes, reasons, finding text and refusal reasons.

Today _journal_io's redaction section answers structural fields before row_hash() and leaves free prose to the after-the-fact detector, tools/check-committed-pii.py. By the time the detector reports, the row is chained, and only a BASELINE row can account for it.

The fix sits at the one place every row passes before it is hashed. A free-text value is checked there for the path shapes the detector reads as machine identity: a home directory under /Users/<name> or /home/<name>, a Windows user directory, and this checkout's absolute root.
- A path inside this repository is rewritten to its repo-relative spelling. That is the structural answer the section already uses.
- Anything else of those shapes is refused before the row is written. The refusal names the field and the shape, never echoes the value, and says how to say it instead (a repo-relative path, or <scratchpad>/<home> placeholders).
- The detector's patterns are not copied. Share them with tools/check-committed-pii.py through one definition, if the layer rule allows; otherwise state why the two must agree, and add a case that holds them equal.

Cases:
- A note quoting a home path is refused and the journal is unchanged.
- An in-repo absolute path is written repo-relative.
- Ordinary prose that mentions 'home' or 'Users' as words is written unchanged.
- The refusal text does not contain the value.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__journal_io.py: a free-text field quoting a home-directory path is refused before the row is hashed and the journal is unchanged, an in-repo absolute path is written repo-relative, and prose using 'home' or 'Users' as words is written unchanged

outcome.technical:
_journal_io's redaction section, at the one place every row passes before row_hash: _MACHINE_PATH_SHAPES (posix-home and windows-user-path, moved here from the detector) with MACHINE_PATH_SHAPES as a public alias for it and MACHINE_PATH_TOKEN_START, the token boundary both readers use; _checkout_roots(project) (the root as written and resolved, never the filesystem root); _in_repo_relative rewrites each absolute token inside the repo through repo_relative_or_token (only tokens os.path.isabs calls absolute on this platform); machine_path_shape(text, roots) asks about the checkout root first, then each shape; free_text(project, field, value) rewrites, then raises ValueError if a shape remains, naming the field (summary, details.reason, details.changes[3].to) and the shape, never the value, and saying to write a repo-relative path or <home>/... / <scratchpad>/... . _normalise runs it on summary and normalise_details on every value except cwd (already a token) and the command facts, before _clip and row_hash, so hook rows are covered as well as CLI verbs. tools/check-committed-pii.py imports the shared definition (DETECTORS built from _journal_io.MACHINE_PATH_SHAPES and the token start), so the writer and the detector read one pattern set. Limits stated: append() still swallows the refusal and returns False, so a verb calling append() drops the row and its message (surfacing it needs caller files); a repo-relative path beginning home/<name> or Users/<name> is refused (over-refusal); ft6's checkout-root shape assertion is skipped on Windows. Cost measured twice with a gap: _normalise about 30-32 µs per row, free_text about 10-11 µs; bench-hooks --gate green.
Tests: test__journal_io ft1-ft7 (a home path in a note refused with the journal unchanged; an in-repo absolute path written repo-relative; prose using 'home' and 'Users' as words written unchanged; the refusal does not echo the value; the checkout root refused; the detector's rows are the writer's own objects). outcome.descriptive: A note, outcome or reason that quotes a home directory or this checkout's full path is now refused before it becomes a permanent journal row, and an absolute path inside the repository is written repository-relative, with the writer and the privacy check sharing one definition of what counts.

tasks.title: a machine path in a journal row is redacted when the plugin wrote it, and refused before any write when a caller typed it
tasks.description:
Fixes review findings P108-R1 and P108-R2 (high), P108-R3 and P108-R4. They concern the machine-path rule on journal rows.

Split the rule by who wrote the text.

- Text the plugin builds itself. This covers hook rows (journal-writes' rendered changes), program output (scoped-commit withdrawal reasons, verdict sentences, close-phase basis) and anything else not typed by a caller. A machine path there is REDACTED in place, the same way redacted_text already treats program output: the token becomes OUTSIDE_TOKEN or a named marker. The row is still written. A hook or verb never drops its own row because of what a value contains.

- Free text a caller hands a verb. This covers note text, outcomes, reasons, finding text and the panel's free-text saves. The check is public (for example _journal_io.check_free_text(project, field, value)). Each verb calls it BEFORE it writes the plan, the shard or the panel save. When the check fails, the verb refuses with a non-zero exit and the field/shape/remedy text, and neither the manifest nor the journal takes the value. The verbs are audit-task (note, done, cancel, block, reopen, finding, bug-add and every other free-text flag), set-priority, derive-phase-gate and the panel's write path. Any append that still fails carries its reason into journaledWhy, never silently.

- The checkout-root shape requires a token start before the root as well as after it, so a short root (/src, /app, /repo, /workspace) never matches a relative path or URL containing that segment. A relative 'home/<x>' at the start of a token is flagged by the detector only. The writer does not refuse it, because a repository can hold a home/ directory.

Cases:
- A journal-writes manifest edit whose value holds a home path still yields a manifest.edit row, and the row does not contain the path.
- A withdrawal reason quoting an outside .git path is written tokenised.
- `audit-task note` with a home path exits non-zero, leaves the shard unchanged and names the field.
- The panel save of such a value is refused before writing.
- A short-root fixture writes 'lib/src/foo.ts' and a URL unchanged.

plugins/audit/tests/test__journal_io.py: a withdrawal reason quoting an outside path is written tokenised, and a short checkout root never matches a relative path or URL containing that segment

outcome.technical: _journal_io.py splits the machine-path rule by who wrote the text. check_free_text(project, field, value) judges caller text as typed and returns None or a refusal naming the field, the shape and the remedy, never the value; redacted_free_text(project, value) is for the plugin's own text and never raises: in-repo absolute paths become repo-relative, any token still carrying a machine path becomes OUTSIDE_TOKEN, and a shape crossing token boundaries replaces the whole value. free_text is removed; _normalise and normalise_details redact instead of raising, so a hook or verb never loses its own row over a value. machine_path_shape needs a token start before the checkout root as well as after it, and the writer's posix-home shape needs a leading separator, so a short root no longer matches relative paths or URLs; the detector still reads the same pattern objects. append_why and append_from_cli_why return the path or (False, reason); append and append_from_cli wrap them. audit-task.py: resolve_briefs runs check_free_text on every prose flag after the stdin read and before the lock, so neither the shard nor the journal takes a refused value; _finding_problems applies the same check to issue and resolution for --findings-file batches; every 'did NOT take' and 'not journaled' line prints the reason. set-priority.py and derive-phase-gate.py take the same append path and print the reason (derive-phase-gate --json adds journaledWhy and journaledReason when a row failed). _panel_write.py builds the journaled block once (journal_block) and refuses a change whose new value carries a machine path before the write, in both the composition and config writers; only the new value is judged, so a save can still remove an old one. The failure reason travels in a new journaledReason key because the panel toast and its pin compare journaledWhy to the exact word. One forward-only BASELINE row in check-committed-pii.py covers a chained journal row that quotes the task's own relative example. tasks.title: a write inside bash -c, eval, cp/mv/install or an interpreter journal append gets the bare form's verdict
tasks.description:
Fixes review findings P108-R6 and P108-R8. They are real bypasses at the deny tier.

guard-secrets-read's shell-write arm also reads three things it misses today:
- the command inside a `bash -c` / `sh -c` / `zsh -c` argument and an `eval` argument;
- the destination operand of cp, mv and install;
- for the journal, an interpreter write (python3 -c / a heredoc program that opens a journal file for writing or appending).

- `bash -c "sed -i ... src/app.py"`
- `eval "sed -i ..."`
- `sh -c "sed -i ... <journal>"`
- `python3 -c "open('<journal>','a')..."`
- `cp notes.md <journal>`
- `cp x src/app.py`

The allow twins stay allowed:
- `bash -c "ls src"`
- `eval "echo hi"`
- `cp src/app.py /tmp/x`
- a program that only reads the journal
